mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which lowers real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rise < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs predicts stronger consumer demand, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the PAYEMS increase, or the effect size is not significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP demand) grows quarter-over-quarter by more than 3%, it indicates robust consumer and business demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > (current value + 3%) in the next quarter
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index by more than 5% in a month signals supply-side weakness, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (current value - 5%) in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining RSAFS (reserves) of over 100 million dollars suggest tightening liquidity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < (current value - 100,000,000) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the signal is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE (unemployment) and HOUST (housing starts) above their prior month averages by at least 0.2% and 10%, respectively, creates a labor market and housing expansion synergy that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > (current value + 0.2%) AND HOUST > (current value + 10%) in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or proxies move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL inflation above 4%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days are expected to be negative due to equity discounting for higher future costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or inflation decays rapidly enough to reverse the effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months indicates labor market tightening, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as investors anticipate wage growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or the trend reverses before the horizon.
